cells.tense: You are sharing the strength you carry, and by measure, not by spill.
cells.ask: Offer one thing that took years to earn to someone just starting, and let it fly.
cells.core:
You steady people in the middle of what gets handed down — the practices, the language, the things worth keeping. Strength moves through you to whoever's near it, and it moves the right amount. You give what you have and you don't strip yourself doing it. What people take from you, they can actually carry. The traditions you pass on stay alive in their hands because you handed them at the weight they could hold.

What this balance can feed next is a direction. Enough comes back from the giving now that you can pick which way it all grows. Choose the one you want handing forward, and steer there. It is not a demand; it is the door the giving has opened, and you are the one standing in it.
cells.sheetLine: You share the strength you carry, and you share it by the right measure.
cells.place: where meaning gets handed down between people

cells.tense: You are carrying what isn't yours yet, spending strength you haven't been asked to spend.
cells.ask: Name what's actually fair to give right now — then give that, and let the rest land on its own.
cells.core:
You hold people up in what gets passed down between them — that part works. You know the traditions, you know who needs steadying, and your hands are good at it. When this runs well, your strength goes exactly to the ones who need it and no further, and what you give comes back around without anyone keeping score. What's off is the size of the load you pick up before anyone hands it over. You feel the need coming and you're already answering it.

The way back is your own felt sense of what's fair. Not a ledger you keep, just the plain knowing of what's yours to put down and what belongs to the next pair of hands. Give by that knowing and the carrying goes light again.
cells.sheetLine: You're shouldering loads nobody has handed you yet.

cells.tense: You pulled your hands back from the work of passing things on, and the room you left is still standing.
cells.ask: Test one piece of what's been handed down by using it with someone and seeing what holds — commitment shows in the trying, not the deciding.
cells.core:
When this goes well, your strength moves outward into what gets shared. You put something into the hands of others and it holds them. The practices you carry find someone to carry them next, and the giving is the whole point. There is a shape to it, and you know it.

The line went quiet. Not because the strength left, but because you stopped finishing things out loud where people could take them. The way back runs through letting something run its course with someone else in it. Pick one thing you carry, use it in front of another person, and let the end of it come. The finished thing is the only thing that can be handed over.
cells.sheetLine: The strength is there; the offering into shared hands has stopped.
cells.place: where meaning gets handed down between people

cells.tense: You are already passing things down, and describing it as though nobody in particular did the passing.
cells.ask: Say plainly, once, that this is the direction you chose — name the thing you're building toward as yours.
cells.core:
What you live inside passes to others through you — the words, the habits, the things you keep going. That current is real, and it is running right now. When it is going well, you know you chose what to hand on and you say so. The people around you get something with a person behind it.

What's missing is the claim. You frame it as though the practice carried itself, or the times carried it, and none of it had an author. The name on it is yours. Point at one thing you've been handing down and say out loud that you picked it and you're steering it. The current gets a direction a person can follow.
cells.sheetLine: The handing-down is running. You just haven't said it's you doing it.
